segments.narration: She cut the labels out of every piece of clothing. Every prescription, every maker's mark, scraped off or burned away.
Hikers found her on the twenty-ninth of November, 1970, in Isdalen valley outside Bergen. Her face was gone, her clothes scorched.
Police traced two suitcases to Bergen railway station. Wigs, foreign currency, a coded notebook, a prescription bottle with no name.
Decoded, the notebook was an itinerary. She had crossed Europe under at least eight passports, calling herself Belgian, writing in German or French.
In 2017, isotopes in her teeth put her childhood near Nuremberg, born around 1930. Nobody has matched that to a name.
